names.note: His own name, read out of doxologia.ro's line for 8 iunie, «Sfinții Mucenici Nicandru și Marcian», which names two men.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 8 Ιουνίου, «Άγιοι Νίκανδρος και Μαρκιανός», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s body for 25. мај ст. ст., not out of its heading, which is „Свети мученици Пасикрат, Валентион, Јулије и други“ and does not name him: „По том Никандар би изведен пред префекта Максима“. **The nominative is restored out of that sentence and that is a reading, not a regex** — the form in the text is already nominative there, and it is given bare, with no rank word attached to it anywhere in the entry. **Measured, and the result was not the expected one**: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for the bare «Никандар», so this is the first folder to hold that exact string — **and `nicander-of-egypt-15-march` holds «Никандар Мисирац», a fuller form of the same name, which `corpus-gate.mjs` does NOT fold onto it**: the gate was run and prints no «никандар» row at all, folding on the whole stored string rather than on a leading word. What it does carry for this name are two settled `·` rows, on the Greek «νικανδροσ» and the Romanian «nicandru», both of which already list this folder. The prediction that a bare form beside a fuller one would raise a `?` row was made before the gate was run and was wrong; this is what was measured. **There is no fuller form to prefer**: this entry gives the name bare in the body and nothing in its heading, and the place would have to be composed from the display name, which is not a reading. The fold is entered on purpose, as the bare «Михаил» was on 23 May. Note the Serbian vowel: this book writes «Никандар» where the Russian calendar writes «Никандр», and the two are not the same string.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 8 iunie — «Sfinții Mucenici Nicandru și Marcian»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 8ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιοι Νίκανδρος και Μαρκιανός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day as the folder's Romanian row, and carries the two men on one page with a head line each and no year against either. It is plainly the same pair: the two soldiers who confessed Christ before the governor Maximus, were held twenty days in prison, torn with iron claws, hung head down over a fire, salted and vinegared, rubbed with rough tile, had their mouths and faces crushed with stones and their tongues cut out, and were beheaded. saint.gr names the governor Maximus and gives no city and no year, so the folder's existing `dates` are left as they are and `locations` stays out. No hymn is printed. Note that the same day's listing carries a second, separate «Άγιος Νίκανδρος», whose own page says it is unknown whether he is the same as this one; no folder and no row was made for that entry, and the reader's report says why. Of him the page says that his wife stood by the tortures and encouraged him to bear them willingly.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 07.06.2026 (25. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Пасикрат, Валентион, Јулије и други“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry. **His name is not in the heading at all — it is in the body** — so this row exists because the day was read and not because anything scored it: the sweep scores a heading and the day list reads the corpus, and **neither finds a companion the heading does not name**. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23, 24 and 25 May is. **THE COMPANY, AND HOW IT WAS TOLD FROM THE OTHER DAYS.** The heading enumerates three — „Пасикрат, Валентион, Јулије“ — and „и други“ after them, and the body names two more, **Никандар** and **Маркијан**, so five men of this entry have folders and all five get a row. **The corpus keeps them on three different days of three different calendars**: `passicrates-of-durostorum` and `valentine-of-durostorum` on 24 April, `julius-the-veteran` on the Romanian 27 May and the Greek 26 May, and `nicander-of-durostorum` and `marcian-of-durostorum` on 8 June. **Not one of them was found by `sr-namesweep.mjs` scoring this heading** — it scores only the first name of an enumerated company, which is its fourth known failure mode — **and not one of them is on the day list for the menologion 25/5 either**, the corpus keeping none of them on that day. They were found by `ls saints | grep -iE 'pasicrat|valent|nicander|marcian|julius' and by grepping the corpus for the entry’s own uncommon proper name, Durostorum, which returned twelve folders at once. **The grep beat both instruments again**, and the misspelling is why the first grep missed one: the corpus stores him `passicrates-of-durostorum`, with two s. **«Доростолу Македонском» AGAINST MOESIA, RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED.** The Prologue puts Durostorum in **Macedonia**; doxologia puts it in the Roman province of Moesia Inferior and saint.gr in Moesia. **No `locations` was written or changed on any of the five.** **«око 302» IS REFUSED ON ALL FIVE, AND FOR THREE DIFFERENT REASONS.** It is the only year this entry gives, it is approximate, and it is stated of the heading’s company and not of any one man. For `julius-the-veteran` it **narrows**: his folder holds 284 to 311 off the Romanian page, and a reader before this one had already refused saint.gr’s flat 302 for the same reason, writing „the year is the Greek’s; this folder’s dating stays the interval the Romanian page allows“ — this book agreeing with saint.gr changes nothing, two books inside a range still not narrowing it. For `nicander-of-durostorum` and `marcian-of-durostorum` it would **widen an `attested` 298 with an approximation**, and a „око“ is not a source for an endpoint. For `passicrates-of-durostorum` and `valentine-of-durostorum` **it is the Prologue’s second answer to a question the Prologue has already answered differently**, and that is the finding of the day, below. **NO DATE ON ANY OF THE FIVE WAS TOUCHED.** **A SECOND DAY ON A CALENDAR THAT KEPT HIM ON NONE**: his `serbian` row was `undocumented`, and the Prologue keeps him on 25 May where doxologia and saint.gr keep him on 8 June. **The Prologue’s own Julian 06-08 was read before this row was written and does not keep him** — it prints Ephraim of Antioch, Zosimus of Phoenicia and Theodore Stratelates — **so the 25 May is this book’s only day for him and no later reader is barred from anything.** That check was made because §4’s warning about writing a lesser day onto an `undocumented` row applies exactly here. **WHAT IS NEW IS ONE EXCHANGE, AND THE REST CORROBORATES.** saint.gr already gave this folder the governor Maximus, the twenty days in prison, the tortures, and **the wife who encouraged her husband to bear them**; the Prologue confirms all of it in two sentences and adds **the dialogue**: that **when Nicander was brought before the prefect Maximus his wife encouraged him to die for Christ, and that Maximus said to her angrily „Глупа бабо, теби се хоће бољи муж!“** — stupid old woman, you want a better husband — **and that she answered „Ако ти тако мислиш о мени, нареди, нека мене сад погубе пре мога мужа!“**, if that is what you think of me, give the order, let them kill me before my husband. **Neither other page has the prefect speak to her or her answer him.** It also makes him one of a company of five, which neither other page does. `martyr` and `soldier` are both corroborated. **Nicander’s wife gains no folder and no row**: she is unnamed in all three books, and a wife is a kinship the body narrates, so the row is owed and refused only for want of anyone to write it for. **The prefect Maximus gains nothing** by the coordinator’s third ruling — the martyrdom belongs to him and not to the persecutor, the reading made on 20 May — and `maximus-of-marcianopolis` and the corpus’s other Maximi are other men. **No `locations`.** The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
